extra.message: User-controlled POST parameter 'user_id' (user_id_form) is interpolated directly into a raw SQL string via % formatting and passed to User.objects.raw(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. "' OR '1'='1") to read/modify the users table.

hits_by_ip() builds a raw SQL statement with % formatting using 'col' and 'ip', both of which come from request.GET in admin_analytics (app/views/admin/views.py:88-98), and executes it via cursor.execute(). Both the selected columns and the ip_address filter are injectable, allowing arbitrary SQL execution.

os.system() is called with a shell command built via string formatting that includes orig_file.name, which is the attacker-controlled uploaded filename (request.FILES['myfile'].name). A crafted filename such as 'x; rm -rf /' results in arbitrary OS command execution.

reset_password() passes the attacker-controlled POST field 'user' through base64.b64decode() directly into pickle.loads(). Deserializing untrusted pickle data allows arbitrary remote code execution on the server.
api_index() calls eval() on the 'class' GET parameter supplied by the remote user. This allows arbitrary Python code execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: api_id() calls eval() on the 'class' GET parameter supplied by the remote user. This allows arbitrary Python code execution on the server.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: download() concatenates the user-controlled GET parameter 'name' onto BASE_DIR and opens the resulting path with file(). A value like '../../etc/passwd' allows reading arbitrary files from the server filesystem.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: save_data() joins the attacker-controlled uploaded_file.name onto data_path with no sanitization and saves the file there via default_storage.save(). A filename containing '../' allows writing arbitrary files outside the intended directory (arbitrary file write).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: sessions_index() redirects to 'path', which is taken directly from the POST parameter 'path' (line 27) with no validation. An attacker can supply an external URL (e.g. https://evil.com) to redirect victims after login, enabling phishing.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: safe_name() wraps the user-controlled first_name in mark_safe(), and it is rendered unescaped in the site-wide navigation template (template/layouts/shared/nav_loggedin.html:23 '{{ current_user.safe_name }}'). An attacker can store a script in their first name (via signup or account update) and achieve stored XSS against every page.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: admin_dashboard() is protected only by user_is_authenticated and never checks current_user.is_admin, so any authenticated non-admin user can access the admin dashboard.
admin_get_user() only requires authentication and never verifies is_admin, allowing any authenticated user to view arbitrary user records by selected_id.

admin_delete_user() deletes an arbitrary user (user.delete() at line 43) with only a user_is_authenticated check and no is_admin verification. Any logged-in user can delete any account, including administrators.

admin_update_user() updates an arbitrary user's attributes and password with only a user_is_authenticated check and no is_admin verification. Any authenticated user can reset another user's (including an admin's) password, leading to account takeover.

User.objects.filter(...).update(**data) blindly applies every key from request.POST as a model attribute. An attacker can include fields such as is_admin=true to escalate privileges (mass assignment) on any user.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: admin_get_all_users() returns User.objects.all() to any authenticated user because only user_is_authenticated is enforced and is_admin is never checked, exposing the full user list.
admin_analytics() exposes the analytics dataset (IPs, referrers, user agents) to any authenticated user since only user_is_authenticated is enforced and is_admin is never checked.

user_work_info_index() fetches User.objects.get(id=user_id) using the user_id from the URL without verifying it matches the authenticated user. Any authenticated user can view any other user's work info, which includes income and SSN (template/users/work_info/index.html:36).

The cleartext SSN is exposed to anyone who can view the page or intercept the response.

extra.message: user_message() fetches Message.objects.get(pk=message_id) using only the message_id from the URL with no check that the message belongs to the current user. Any authenticated user can read (GET) or delete (DELETE) any other user's private messages.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: user_pay() deletes Pay.objects.get(id=pay_id) using only the pay_id from the URL without checking ownership. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's direct-deposit/pay records.

extra.message: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 (hash_password(); authentication compares against hashlib.md5 at line 107). MD5 is fast and unsalted, so stolen password hashes are trivially crackable via rainbow tables/brute force.

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: The password reset token is simply str(user_id) + '-' + MD5(email) with no secret, randomness, or expiry. Anyone who knows a victim's user_id and email can compute a valid token and take over the account via the password reset flow.

cwe: CWE-640: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password

extra.message: generate_token() creates the persistent session auth_token as MD5(email + random.randint(1,1000000)). The token is unsalted MD5 over a low-entropy value (only ~20 bits of randomness plus a known email), making session tokens brute-forceable/predictable.

cwe: CWE-330: Use of Insufficiently Random Values

extra.message: The login flow returns distinct error messages for a nonexistent email ('Email incorrect!') versus a wrong password ('Password incorrect!'), allowing attackers to enumerate valid user email addresses.

forgot_password() returns different messages depending on whether the submitted email exists in the system ('An email was sent...' vs 'We do not have the email in our system'), enabling user/email enumeration.
Django SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source control. Anyone with access to the repository can forge signed cookies/tokens and compromise session integrity.

The AES key (settings.KEY) used to encrypt SSNs and bank account numbers (app/models/utils.py:33) is a hardcoded static value in source control. Anyone with repo access can decrypt all stored sensitive data.

ACCESS_TOKEN_SALT is hardcoded. API access tokens are computed as SHA1(salt + ':' + user_id) (app/views/api/users/views.py:59-61), so anyone with the repo can forge valid API tokens for any user_id and bypass API authentication.
Database credentials are hardcoded (USER 'root', PASSWORD 'password') in docker_settings.py and committed to source control.
DEBUG = True in the main settings module. In production this exposes detailed stack traces, settings, and the Django debug toolbar information to attackers.
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] disables Django's Host header validation, permitting HTTP Host header attacks (cache poisoning, password reset poisoning).
save_data() calls uploaded_file.read(), loading the entire uploaded file into memory at once with no size limit. A large upload can exhaust server memory, causing denial of service.

The session auth_token cookie is set without httponly=True or secure=True (both the 'remember' and default branches). The token is accessible to JavaScript (amplifying XSS into session theft) and can be sent over plaintext HTTP.
